title: Core Emergency Ultrasound
short: One day of hands-on scanning that covers every core point-of-care ultrasound application in the RCEM curriculum.
seoTitle: Core Emergency Ultrasound Course (Level 1, RCEM curriculum)
seoDescription: One-day Level 1 point-of-care ultrasound course for emergency clinicians. eFAST, AAA, echo in life support, shock assessment, vascular access and fascia iliaca block. Small groups, consultant faculty.
audience: Emergency medicine trainees working towards RCEM ultrasound sign-off
Acute and internal medicine doctors starting point-of-care ultrasound
Advanced clinical practitioners, physician associates and GPs working in urgent care
Consultants and SAS doctors refreshing or formalising their skills
overview: This course gives you the knowledge and the hands-on time to start scanning with confidence. Each module follows the same pattern: a short, focused talk, live demonstration, then supervised scanning on healthy models and simulators.

The content maps to the core point-of-care ultrasound applications in the RCEM 2021 curriculum. You leave with a certificate, a logbook template and a clear plan for collecting supervised scans and gaining sign-off in your own department.

modules.name: Physics and knobology
modules.text: How the image forms, probe choice, depth, gain and focus, and the artefacts you need to recognise.

modules.name: eFAST
modules.text: Free fluid in the abdomen and pelvis, pericardial fluid, haemothorax and pneumothorax in the trauma patient.

modules.name: Abdominal aortic aneurysm
modules.text: A systematic scan of the abdominal aorta, measuring it correctly and knowing when the scan is incomplete.

modules.name: Echo in life support
modules.text: Focused echo during cardiac arrest, timed within the ALS algorithm without delaying compressions.

modules.name: Shock assessment
modules.text: A structured approach to the shocked patient, combining heart, lungs, IVC, abdomen and aorta.

modules.name: Vascular access
modules.text: Real-time needle guidance for peripheral and central venous access on high-fidelity phantoms.

modules.name: Fascia iliaca block
modules.text: Ultrasound-guided regional anaesthesia for hip fractures, practised on phantoms with safety checks.

modules.name: Governance and sign-off
modules.text: Logbooks, image storage, reflections and the RCEM route to entrustment, so your learning continues after the day.

programme.item: Welcome. Physics, knobology and image optimisation
Hands-on: probe handling and image optimisation
Abdominal aortic aneurysm: talk and scanning
Echo in life support, with simulated arrest scenarios
Vascular access and fascia iliaca block on phantoms
Governance, logbooks and the sign-off pathway. Questions

includes: Small groups at every scanning station
Healthy volunteer models, simulators and vascular phantoms

faqs.q: Do I need any previous ultrasound experience?
faqs.a: No. The course starts from first principles. If you already scan, the structured approach and supervised practice still strengthen your technique.

faqs.q: Does this course give me RCEM sign-off?
faqs.a: No single course does. Sign-off comes from supervised scans, reflections and assessment in your own department. This course covers the learning element and shows you how to complete the rest.
Emergency medicine consultants and experienced point-of-care ultrasound practitioners, led by the Course Director.

faqs.q: Can I use my study leave budget?
faqs.a: Yes. We provide an invoice and certificate for study leave and appraisal.
